final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor presented no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrower framing is more accurate than the original clean-certification posture, but it is still not enough for compliant_with_caveats here because the unresolved issue is not merely a disclosure note to accompany launch; it is an unmet policy predicate. The admissible evidence shows a 1.3 percentage point miss in a segment named in two paid pilot commitments, an open legal question on whether disclosure is required, and a policy requiring disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch for material limitations affecting named launch use cases. On this record, operational readiness is supported, but compliance with the disclosure condition is not. Treating the issue as a caveat rather than a satisfied condition remains unsupported.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the small-business onboarding limitation was disclosed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk-acceptance record covering this specific limitation.
The affected segment is named in two paid pilot commitments, which supports materiality under the policy text.
Open legal review leaves the disclosure predicate unresolved.
Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness only; they do not satisfy the separate disclosure requirement for a material limitation.
